positive_controls.argument: Architecture analysis identifies which failure domains, resource limits and coupling determine whether the objective is achievable and whether release changes can affect it in the assumed way.
Actual deployment and environment correspondence determines which version and exposure the budget observations concern, preventing credit from an unrelated or mixed state.
Envelope limits and representative-configuration assumptions restrict where the service objective and observations can support a claim and when changed conditions require new evidence.
Hazard scenarios and binding risk constraints identify where ordinary service-budget trading is inapplicable and which additional assurance or prevention conditions must remain hard constraints.
The operational owner, transition configuration and support conditions establish where and by whom the reliability policy can be enforced during the real cutover.
Measured recovery capability, state compatibility and response-resource limits determine whether the release policy's assumed containment or restoration time is credible.
Support capabilities, dependency end dates and retirement options constrain which service objectives remain feasible and which release policies can actually be sustained.
The consequence and commitment analysis determines whether service-budget reasoning applies at all and which separate hard constraints or recovery assumptions must limit it.
Rejecting the unrestricted late-cost rule requires the release trade-off to use its actual objective, loss window and authority instead of an assumed phase penalty.
